structured.approach: I followed the DE-02 procedure in the data-engineering-steps skill. First I read feat.tasks to find the lane's tasks. Both are in ap_pipeline: TSK-01, the paid_date parsing in transform.py, and TSK-02, a new pure function delays_by_vendor in delays.py with no I/O. org.permission_table is restricted, so I compared those tasks against it only through the tool view. That view says no secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline. To confirm the code needs none, I read ingest.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json, and I searched the whole checkout for environment-variable, credential and network patterns. Nothing matched. I then wrote task.secrets_scope with names only: an empty scope for each branch (feature/<story>, dev, main) and no access request. The step was a small lookup, so I did it directly without a helper subagent. I listed two non-blocking follow-ups: scheduler and notification credentials for later steps, and whether there are environments beyond the branches.

claims.text: The Data Engineering lane's tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-02 adds a new pure function, delays_by_vendor, in src/ap_pipeline/delays.py with no I/O.
The tasks add no new technology, only the Python 3.9 standard library (feat.design DD-1).
Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding. Coding builds on synthetic v3 rows.
No secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository.
parse_feed parses CSV text with csv.DictReader over io.StringIO. It opens no connection and reads no credential.
pipeline.run chains parse_feed, to_model and quality_report on the CSV text passed to it. No source system is called.
The pipeline schedule is daily at 02:00, Asia/Kolkata.
ap_pipeline uses the Python 3.9 standard library and has branches main (released), dev (integration) and feature/<story>.
There is no gap between the secrets the DE tasks need and the secrets granted, so no access request was raised.

open_questions: SQ-DE-1 (non-blocking): Will DE-13 (scheduling) or DE-14 (email and Teams notifications) need a scheduler or notification credential? None is needed for TSK-01 or TSK-02, and none is granted. Re-check at those steps.
SQ-DE-2 (non-blocking): Are there deployment environments beyond the main, dev and feature/<story> branches that need their own secret scope? None are named in the inputs.
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope for the Data Engineering lane (ap_pipeline). No secrets are needed or granted, and no access request is required. TSK-01 parses paid_date in transform.py and TSK-02 adds a pure delays_by_vendor function; both use synthetic data and the standard library only. The permission table's tool view grants no secrets for ap_pipeline. A search of the checkout found no environment-variable, credential or network use. The scope is empty for the feature, dev and main branches. Two non-blocking questions remain: credentials for the later scheduling and notification steps (DE-13, DE-14), and environments beyond the branches.
